summary.short: German federal statute creating the Federal Office for Information Security and setting IT-security duties for essential and important entities, domain-name registries and federal agencies, with supervision and fines. Only the table of contents was supplied, so dates and operative text are not verified.
summary.long: The statute (BSIG) is outlined in nine parts. Parts 1 and 2 establish the Federal Office for Information Security with tasks and powers: reporting offices, detection, warnings, information requests, individual orders to telecommunications and digital service providers and ICT product manufacturers, and provision of IT-security products. They also set data-processing and data-subject rights rules. Part 3 sets duties for essential and important entities (sector annexes 1 and 2): risk-management measures, incident reporting, registration, notification, management training, proof duties for critical installations, a prohibition on the use of critical components, and duties for federal administration bodies. Part 4 concerns domain-name registration databases and access. Part 5 covers certification, conformity assessment and a voluntary IT-security label. Part 6 contains ordinance powers, restrictions of fundamental rights and the Office's reporting duties. Part 7 sets supervision and enforcement measures. Part 8 contains fines. Part 9 contains application and transitional rules. The supplied document is a table of contents only. Obligation content, thresholds, dates and penalty amounts are not in the text and are not coded. The start date is not stated in the outline; section 66 holds the application rule.
